claims.statement: Binding Tariff Information is a legal classification decision issued by EU customs authorities, generally valid across the EU for three years and binding on authorities and the holder.
Tariff classification determines customs duty and can also determine non-tariff measures such as licences, restrictions and origin-related requirements.

contrary_evidence: Valid and invalid BTI decisions are already public in the EBTI database, so defensibility must come from confidential fact patterns, workflow distribution and outcome data rather than public rulings.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: white-label inside freight forwarders and customs agencies at the moment a new or ambiguous SKU enters Europe.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: resolve 100 cases in year 1, reach 3 million PLN ARR by year 4, build 3.5 million PLN founder equity and retained cash by year 6, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 7-10.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-3 hours per day with customs opinions provided by contracted specialists.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 55%-80% gross margin after customs-expert review, translation and case support.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 8-16 months if one forwarder supplies repeat cases.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated commercial figures, including capital_required_pln: 2,000-12,000 PLN per complex classification case plus 1,000-5,000 PLN monthly forwarder workspace.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: repeat follows new SKUs, rule changes and product modifications; no case frequency or retention is validated.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Consented private mappings between product facts, questions, rulings, appeals and landed-cost outcomes improve retrieval and expert efficiency
fingerprint.customer: EU importers and freight forwarders handling novel or ambiguous products
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label insertion into forwarder and customs-agent onboarding of new products
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Structured product evidence, expert review and BTI application support, without pretending to issue a binding ruling
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer or forwarder pays for a reviewed case pack and ongoing workflow access
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new SKU lacks a defensible tariff classification or faces a classification dispute

founder_fit: Strong match for structured evidence retrieval and AI-assisted analysis.
Expert review can be contracted while the founder builds the data system.
risks: Incorrect product facts lead to an invalid or harmful classification.
Public AI tools commoditise simple classification research.

structure.commercial_archetype: Expert decision network with case-outcome data cooperative
structure.control_point: Forwarder channel agreements and contractual rights to reuse de-identified product-description, decision and exception outcomes
structure.critical_dependency: Qualified customs expertise, confidentiality-safe data rights, accurate product facts and client acceptance of the BTI process

thesis: Embed with freight forwarders and customs representatives to structure difficult product-classification cases and, with client permission, retain anonymised product-feature, ruling, appeal and realised-cost outcomes. The control point is a private case-outcome network and forwarder distribution, while qualified customs professionals remain responsible for advice and representation.
title: Customs Classification Outcome Cooperative
uncertainties: Scope of activities requiring customs-representative credentials
Value of private outcomes beyond public EBTI records
